arxiv-2101-06499.title: Equilibrium of an Arbitrary Bunch Train in the Presence of Multiple Resonator Wake Fields
arxiv-2101-06499.creator: Robert Warnock
arxiv-2101-06499.description: Abstract A higher harmonic cavity (HHC), used to cause bunch lengthening for an increase in the Touschek lifetime, is a feature of several fourth generation synchrotron light sources. The desired bunch lengthening is complicated by the presence of required gaps in the bunch train.

arxiv-2209-04788.title: Asymmetric Dark Matter from Gravitational Waves
arxiv-2209-04788.creator: Bartosz Fornal, Erika Pierre
arxiv-2209-04788.description: Abstract We investigate the prospects for probing asymmetric dark matter models through their gravitational wave signatures. We concentrate on a theory extending the Standard Model gauge symmetry by a non-Abelian group, under which leptons form doublets with new fermionic partners, one of them being a dark matter candidate.

arxiv-2211-03715.title: TDC: Towards Extremely Efficient CNNs on GPUs via Hardware-Aware Tucker Decomposition Conference: The 28th ACM SIGPLAN Annual Symposium on Principles and Practice of Parallel Programming; February 25-March 1, 2023; Montreal, QC, Canada The 28th ACM SIGPLAN Annual Symposium on Principles and Practice
arxiv-2211-03715.creator: Lizhi Xiang, Miao Yin, Chengming Zhang, Aravind Sukumaran-Rajam, P. Sadayappan, Bo Yuan, Dingwen Tao
arxiv-2211-03715.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Lizhi Xiang, Miao Yin, Chengming Zhang, Aravind Sukumaran-Rajam, P. Sadayappan, Bo Yuan, Dingwen Tao. Tucker decomposition is one of the SOTA CNN model compression techniques. However, unlike the FLOPs reduction, we observe very limited inference time reduction with Tucker-compressed models using existing GPU software such as cuDNN. To this end, we propose an efficient end-to-end framework that can generate highly accurate and compact CNN models via Tucker decomposition and optimized inference code on GPUs.

arxiv-2308-09556.title: A Principle for Global Optimization with Gradients
arxiv-2308-09556.creator: Nils Müller
arxiv-2308-09556.description: Abstract This work demonstrates the utility of gradients for the global optimization of certain differentiable functions with many suboptimal local minima. To this end, a principle for generating search directions from non-local quadratic approximants based on gradients of the objective function is analyzed.

arxiv-2403-07929.title: Sketching the Heat Kernel: Using Gaussian Processes to Embed Data
arxiv-2403-07929.creator: Anna Gilbert, Kevin O’Neill
arxiv-2403-07929.description: Abstract This paper introduces a novel, non-deterministic method for embedding data in low-dimensional Euclidean space based on computing realizations of a Gaussian process depending on the geometry of the data. This type of embedding first appeared in [ 1 ] as a theoretical model for a generic manifold in high dimensions.

arxiv-2406-18960.title: A Surprisingly Simple yet Effective Multi-Query Rewriting Method for Conversational Passage Retrieval
arxiv-2406-18960.creator: Ivica Kostric, Krisztian Balog
arxiv-2406-18960.description: Abstract . Conversational passage retrieval is challenging as it often requires the resolution of references to previous utterances and needs to deal with the complexities of natural language, such as coreference and ellipsis. To address these challenges, pre-trained sequence-to-sequence neural query rewriters are commonly used to generate a single de-contextualized query based on conversation history.

arxiv-2407-12981.title: Transition to turbulence in the wide-gap spherical Couette system
arxiv-2407-12981.creator: A. Barik 1, S. A. Triana 2, M. Hoff 3, J. Wicht 4
arxiv-2407-12981.description: Abstract The spherical Couette system consists of two differentially rotating concentric spheres with a fluid filled in between. We study a regime where the outer sphere is rotating rapidly enough so that the Coriolis force is important and the inner sphere is rotating either slower or in the opposite direction with respect to the outer sphere.

pmc-11438082.title: Effect of a prolonged slow expiration technique on 24-h food intake in children hospitalized for moderate bronchiolitis: a randomized controlled trial
pmc-11438082.creator: Yann Combret, Margaux Machefert, Mélody Couet, Tristan Bonnevie, Francis-Edouard Gravier, Timothée Gillot, Pascal Le Roux, Roger Hilfiker, Clément Medrinal, Guillaume Prieur
pmc-11438082.description: BackgroundChest physiotherapy for airway clearance is not recommended in children hospitalized with bronchiolitis. The updated Cochrane meta-analysis suggests that slow expiratory techniques could slightly improve clinical severity, but the evidence certainty is low and the clinical significance of this change is unknown. We investigated whether the prolonged slow expiration technique (PSET) would impact the 24-h food intake of these children.

pmc-11499753.title: Multicentre study to assess the performance of an artificial intelligence instrument to support qualitative diagnosis of colorectal polyps
pmc-11499753.creator: Keigo Sato, Mizuki Kuramochi, Akihiko Tsuchiya, Akihiro Yamaguchi, Yasuo Hosoda, Norio Yamaguchi, Naohiro Nakamura, Yuki Itoi, Yu Hashimoto, Kengo Kasuga, Hirohito Tanaka, Shiko Kuribayashi, Yoji Takeuchi, Toshio Uraoka
pmc-11499753.description: ObjectiveComputer-aided diagnosis (CAD) using artificial intelligence (AI) is expected to support the characterisation of colorectal lesions, which is clinically relevant for efficient colorectal cancer prevention. We conducted this study to assess the diagnostic performance of commercially available CAD systems.MethodsThis was a multicentre, prospective performance evaluation study.

pmc-12595902.title: ODR1/AtSDR4L alleviates osmotic stress-induced germination arrest via ABA-dependent negative feedback on ABA biosynthesis
pmc-12595902.creator: Ling Ding, Xu Ran, Yuan Cao, Xiangfeng Liu, Yong Xiang, Xi Chen
pmc-12595902.description: BackgroundTo optimize offspring seed survival in fluctuating environments, seed plants have evolved two key adaptive strategies, seed dormancy under favorable conditions and germination arrest under stress, to control germination timing. The phytohormone abscisic acid acts as a master regulator in both processes, exerting precise control over its endogenous levels and signaling to fine-tune this seed-seedling transition.

pmc-13157484.title: Exploring the prospects of artificial intelligence in transforming dental care for special needs groups: mapping the current evidence
pmc-13157484.creator: Mithun Pai, Shweta Yellapurkar, Kavery Chengappa S, Kalyana C Pentapati
pmc-13157484.description: BackgroundThe integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) in providing quality dental care to individuals with special needs has been scarcely explored and holds the potential to be transformative. This study aimed to map the current evidence and research gaps on the application of AI tools in special care dentistry.
